messages:
ci-bot: build #789 failed on linux-x86_64 — unit tests: runtime::serve::test::serve_retry_backpressure_test (flaky)
alex: saw this in the morning, seems to pop up intermittently in the matrix (3/25 runs)
maria: repro log attached in the CI artifact: https://ci.redwood/example/build/789/artifacts/serve_retry_log.txt
sam: quick skim: looks like a race on attempt counters + a non-deterministic ordering of timers. stack: `tokio::timer::wheel::tick` -> retry loop -> serve loop
alex: can someone rerun with `RUST_TEST_THREADS=1` + `--nocapture -Z unstable-options --test-threads=1` to see if it's scheduler-related?
jordan: good idea. also try `--exact` to isolate that test. I'm +1 for forcing single-thread CI run to confirm.
lee: volunteer to kick off a rerun now. re-running job 789 with `env RUST_TEST_THREADS=1 cargo test -p runtime --test serve -- serve_retry_backpressure_test --exact`
ci-bot: re-run started (job 790) — will post results when finished
lee: quick note: I grabbed an intermittent failure trace from the previous artifact. snippet:
```
thread 'serve_retry_backpressure_test' panicked at 'assert_eq!(expected, observed)', src/serve/retries.rs:142
note: expected=1, observed=2
Backtrace:
  0: runtime::serve::retries::handle_attempt
  1: runtime::serve::Worker::poll
  2: runtime::serve::test::serve_retry_backpressure_test
```
maria: that observed=2 is suspicious — could be double-increment on error path. There's a global counter in `retry::metrics::INFLIGHT` that we mutate in two places.
alex: if that's the case we should guard with an atomic fetch_add/fetch_sub and assert on ordering. But still curious why only on linux CI.
sam: I pushed a tiny instrumented patch to my branch (adds debug logging around increment/decrement) — can we bisect to find the change that made it flaky? It's been flaky since ~Feb.
jordan: bisect plan: run `git bisect start -- bad HEAD --good v2026-01-15` then run a short test script. If someone can spare cycles, I can write the script to run the test 20x per commit and fail early.
lee: I can run that tonight on a local linux box. putting it on my queue. If anyone has a faster way: maybe add a deterministic seed env like `REDWOOD_TEST_SEED=1234` so we can reproduce locally.
alex: adding a seed is low cost; test harness already reads REDWOOD_TEST_SEED for other tests. could you add it to this test? if it makes repro 100% we open a PR with the seed and the fix.
maria: if it's a real race, seeding won't fix, just make repro more consistent. still fine for bisect.
lee: update: started bisect run at 4387654340. will ping with first red commit.
ci-bot: job 790 finished — flaky test still failed on single-thread run.
lee: thanks — that suggests it's not scheduler-level. continuing bisect. next update in ~2h.
alex: low-effort mitigation: add test retry on CI (rerun flaky test once) while we debug? Ops: we should avoid masking real regressions. leaning against.
jordan: agree, let's not mask. instead add a short flaky-check action that aggregates failures for the last 72h.
maria: FYI I left comments on sam's PR with two suggestions: (1) make counter ops atomic, (2) ensure early returns don't skip decrement. little change, should be quick.
sam: thanks — I'll land a small fix in the morning and link to bisect result.
lee: bisect found first bad commit: f3a9c2d (concurrent retry refactor) — reproduces 8/20 runs on my box. posting exact bisect log: https://ci.redwood/bisect/lee/4387654321/log.txt
alex: great find. can you open a PR against main with the atomic change + extra test to cover double-decrement? mark as a hotfix with description.
lee: will do. PR will reference this thread. will also add `REDWOOD_TEST_SEED` entry for local repro.
maria: thanks everyone. if the PR passes CI I'll merge and watch for regressions. closing the loop after merge. :rocket:
alex: thanks all :thumbsup:
